recommendation.title: Clear the drain path before replacing parts
recommendation.summary: The safest first repair is to inspect the drain filter, drain hose, and pump inlet for a blockage. The symptom pattern fits a clog more strongly than an electrical pump failure.

causes.name: Blocked drain filter
causes.evidence: Standing water plus a completed wash cycle usually points to debris trapped before the pump.

causes.name: Kinked or clogged drain hose
causes.evidence: Slow or absent drainage can happen when the hose is pinched behind the machine.

causes.name: Drain pump obstruction or failure
causes.evidence: A humming sound during drain suggests the pump is powered but may be jammed.

repair_plan.title: Power down and protect the floor
repair_plan.detail: Unplug the washer, turn off water supply valves, and place towels plus a shallow tray near the access panel.

repair_plan.title: Drain residual water
repair_plan.detail: Open the lower service flap and use the emergency drain tube if available. Keep the cap low and drain slowly.

repair_plan.title: Clean the drain filter
repair_plan.detail: Unscrew the filter counterclockwise, remove lint, coins, buttons, or fabric debris, then rinse the filter.

repair_plan.title: Inspect hose and pump impeller
repair_plan.detail: Check the drain hose for kinks. With the filter removed, confirm the pump impeller turns freely.

repair_plan.title: Run a rinse and drain test
repair_plan.detail: Reinstall the filter tightly, restore power, and run a short rinse/drain cycle while watching for leaks.

safety: Unplug the appliance before opening any service panel.
Do not tip the washer alone; water weight can make it unstable.
Stop if you smell burning, see damaged wiring, or the pump housing leaks.

recommendation.title: Isolate the fault before replacing the unit
recommendation.summary: Start by confirming power, inspecting the most accessible serviceable parts, and checking for obvious blockages or loose connections before considering a replacement.

causes.name: Undiagnosed component fault
causes.evidence: Without a matching symptom profile, the fault needs a hands-on inspection to localize.

repair_plan.title: Disconnect power and water
repair_plan.detail: Unplug the appliance and shut off any connected water supply before inspecting.

repair_plan.title: Inspect accessible serviceable parts
repair_plan.detail: Check filters, hoses, seals, and visible connections for blockages, wear, or looseness.

repair_plan.title: Test after each check
repair_plan.detail: Restore power and run a short cycle after each fix to confirm whether the fault is resolved.

safety: Always disconnect power before opening an appliance.
Stop if you find scorched wiring, water near electronics, or a gas smell.
